entities.summary:
Smenkhkare Imyremeshaw was a minor king of the early 13th Dynasty during the late Middle Kingdom, ruling briefly in the 18th century BCE. His reign was largely confined to the Memphis-Faiyum region in Egypt.

Imyremeshaw's existence is mainly documented in the Turin Papyrus, a 5,000-year-old record of ancient Egyptian royal lineage.

His brief reign is thought to have been a power struggle between Imyremeshaw and his predecessor, Pharaoh Sobekneferu.

The consequences of Imyremeshaw's reign are largely unknown, but it is believed that his short-lived rule may have contributed to the eventual collapse of the 13th Dynasty.

Imyremeshaw's legacy is that of a forgotten ruler, lost to the sands of time, leaving behind only a faint record of his existence.

The discovery of Imyremeshaw's name in the Turin Papyrus has shed new light on the mysteries of ancient Egyptian royal succession, highlighting the complexities and intrigues of the Middle Kingdom.

The significance of Imyremeshaw's reign lies in its contribution to our understanding of the late Middle Kingdom's power dynamics and the intricate web of royal relationships that defined this period in Egyptian history.
